Family holidays in Carinthia, Austria

Explore the mountains together. Without the summer crowds.

Our Panorama Lodge is made for families: three bedrooms (yes, with bunk beds), a big table for cosy evenings and a park with a pool and playgrounds. The lake and the mountains are right around the corner.

Bunk beds!

Why spring or autumn?

More time together, less queuing

No queues

Outside July and August it's quiet at the lifts, on the trails and by the lake. More space to explore together.

Half-term friendly

Spring and autumn fit perfectly with May and October half-term. A short, active break in the mountains.

Room for everyone

A detached chalet with three bedrooms. The kids get their own room, you sleep peacefully in the main bedroom.

Everything on the park

Pool, playgrounds and sports pitches on the park, the lake within walking distance. Handy on a rainy day too.

For kids

Something fun for every age

From splashing to climbing: our favourites for kids aged 4 to 16.

Ages 4–8

Splash and discover

  • Aqua Trail on the NassfeldA 1.5 km play trail on the mountain: build dams, play with fountains and climb aboard a real sailing boat. June to September.
  • Pool and playgroundsRight on the park, handy all year round.
  • Adventure park by the lakeA slide into the lake, mini cars and a kids' zone. Late June to mid-September.

Ages 9–12

Speed and adventure

  • Pendolino summer tobogganRide the gondola up and race 2 km down Carinthia's longest summer toboggan run. June to September.
  • Garnitzenklamm gorgeWaterfalls, little bridges and a geo trail through the gorge. Wear sturdy shoes!
  • Paddleboarding and cyclingOut on the lake on a SUP board, or cycling through the flat Gailtal valley.

Ages 13–16

Challenge and views

  • Nassfeld Outdoor ParkRock labyrinth, flying fox and 3D archery. Daily in June and September in good weather, late May and October on request.
  • Climb a real summitReach a summit cross together, with views across the border into Italy.
  • Day out in VillachShopping, ice cream and cafés in the region's biggest town.

Opening times vary by season and year. Check nassfeld.at before you go.

The house

Panorama Lodge

Into the mountains by day, all together around the big wooden table at night. The kids have their own room with bunk beds, you sleep peacefully in the main bedroom. And on the sun terrace you can enjoy a coffee while the children play outside.

Seasons

What to do each season

May half-term

Around Lake Presseggersee

5.9 km on the flat through the reeds, about an hour and a half. Easy for little legs.

Mid-May

Carinthian Hiking Opening

The region opens the hiking season with a festive weekend in the nearby Lesachtal valley.

April–June

Cycling the Gailtal valley

Flat valley routes, ideal for kids on their own bikes. E-bikes can be hired locally.

From June

Aqua Trail and Pendolino

Once the mountain lifts open in June: play on the Aqua Trail first, then toboggan back down.

All spring

Fossil hunting

In the Carnic Alps Geopark you walk across ancient seabed. Who'll find the first fossil?

Dates and opening times vary from year to year. See nassfeld.at for the current programme.

Day trips

Möderndorf, near Hermagor

Garnitzenklamm gorge

A gorge about 4.5 km long with waterfalls, sheer rock walls and emerald pools. Open in the warmer months; some sections need sure footing.

More info ↗

Lake Presseggersee

Paddleboarding on the lake

Glide over the calm, clear water on a SUP board. Lovely on a mild spring or autumn day.

City day out

Villach and Klagenfurt

Two charming Carinthian towns for a day of shopping, cafés and culture.

Winter

Tröpolach

Skiing from the Millennium Express

We always start at the Millennium Express. Tip: rent a ski locker at the bottom so you don't have to carry anything. Then après-ski at Zum Alois.

More info ↗

Practical

Austria

Required in your car

A warning triangle, a high-vis vest for every passenger, an in-date first-aid kit and a motorway vignette (digital from ASFINAG or at a petrol station before the border). Police do sometimes check.
